=== DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html) ===
• Trino 467 Iceberg maintenance procedures are invoked via ALTER TABLE ... EXECUTE, NOT via CALL:
  - `ALTER TABLE iceberg.<schema>.<table> EXECUTE optimize(file_size_threshold => '256MB')` (default 100MB).
  - `ALTER TABLE iceberg.<schema>.<table> EXECUTE expire_snapshots(retention_threshold => '7d')`.
  - `ALTER TABLE iceberg.<schema>.<table> EXECUTE remove_orphan_files(retention_threshold => '7d')`.
• Trino 467 does NOT support the Spark `CALL iceberg.system.<procedure>(...)` form for any of these — pasting it returns 'Procedure not registered'.
• Spark equivalents (run from spark-sql / spark-shell against SparkCatalog):
  - `CALL iceberg.system.rewrite_data_files(table => '<schema>.<table>', options => map('target-file-size-bytes','268435456'))`.
  - `CALL iceberg.system.expire_snapshots(table => '<schema>.<table>', older_than => current_timestamp - interval '7' day, retain_last => 10)`.
  - `CALL iceberg.system.remove_orphan_files(table => '<schema>.<table>', older_than => current_timestamp - interval '3' day, dry_run => true)`.
• Trino has a min-retention floor (default 7d via `iceberg.expire_snapshots.min-retention`) — sub-7d expiry requires either lowering that catalog property or running from Spark.
• Multi-tenant per-tenant DAU: `WHERE tenant_id = ? GROUP BY date_trunc('day', event_ts)` with `COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)` — straightforward composition of r05 Model 2/3 patterns + r23:131 canonical DAU shape.
• Percent-of-column-total: `100.0 * x / SUM(x) OVER ()` — empty `OVER ()` (no PARTITION, no ORDER) makes the window the entire result set, so SUM(x) OVER () is the grand total repeated on every row. `100.0` DECIMAL literal forces decimal division (integer division trap).
• Cumulative running total: `SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)` — running total up to and INCLUDING the current row. ROWS (positional, per-row frame) NOT RANGE (value-based, lumps tied peers) for accumulate-one-at-a-time semantics.
